subject: Pilot qualification recap — recommendations, perf links, and next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@medisys.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot qualification recap — recommendations, perf links, and next steps

Hi Ari —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps for a pilot qualification: 

Call highlights (short):
- Primary objective: automate triage + assisted summaries for incoming clinical claims (low-latency snippets to feed case workers).
- Expected traffic profile: ~120 QPS peak during business hours, average 28 QPS off-peak; typical prompt length ~420 tokens, returned summary ~120 tokens.
- Hard constraints: P95 latency target <= 400ms for single-request path; strict data residency (US) and SOC2 controls required.

Redwood recommendations (starting configuration):
1) Candidate model: rw-infer-phi-1.3 (3B quantized) — best cost/perf for 400–600 token sequences; tested steady-state TPS ~220 for 8-GPU pool, p50 ~85ms, p95 ~360ms under our batching profiles.
2) Higher-fidelity option: optx-13b-qat — higher quality for edge-case clinical language, expect p95 ~520ms at comparable throughput; recommend for fallback where precision matters.
3) Fallback strategy: primary rw-infer-phi-1.3 + automatic re-route to optx-13b-qat when confidence threshold low or hallucination risk detected.

Quality/regression notes: we flagged a subtle paraphrase drift in internal evals on rare claim templates (examples attached). We'll include a small regression test in the pilot (prompt set + golden labels) to detect changes and trigger rollback.

Attached: redwood-performance-profiles-20271004.pdf (one-page summary of TPS and latency percentiles across candidate models) and prompt-set-sample-claims.jsonl (30 representative prompt/label pairs we recommend using for the pilot sanity checks).

Links: Redwood-verified perf profiles: https://drive.redwood.com/s/medisys-pilot/perf-profiles-20271004
Benchmark run (recent spike test): https://redwood.app/benchmarks/runs/20271001-peak-spike

Proposed next steps (please pick dates):
- Confirm pilot scope (3-week limited pilot; data scope + ingress method) — you
- Approve reserved capacity for initial spike window (we recommend 8 GPUs with burst cap). — Medisys
- Set up pilot onboarding call (30–45 min) with Camila (solutions) to walk infra and secrets. — Camila/Evelyn schedule

If that looks good I’ll send a short SOW draft and calendar options.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: (415) 555-0192

Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 18:42:10 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot qualification recap — recommendations, perf links, and next steps

Evelyn —

Appreciate the detailed write-up. A couple clarifying questions before we lock the pilot: 
1) The P95 numbers you shared for rw-infer-phi-1.3 look promising — can you confirm those are for true 99% P95 under our expected payloads (420 tokens in, 120 tokens out) at 120 QPS bursts, not smoothed averages?
2) For data residency: we need all inference nodes in our AWS us-east-1 VPC and KMS integration — is the private deployment option required for that, or can Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering meet our security/compliance?
3) For the regression test: can we add one real-sample redaction step so PHI never leaves our environment during onboarding? We can provide a small synthetic set to start if needed.

Also please send any cost estimates for the 3-week pilot (reserved burst + data egress) so procurement can triage.

Thanks — I’m free Tue morning for a quick follow.

—Ari
Ari Kaplan
Head of AI Ops | Medisys.ai
ari.kaplan@medisys.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@medisys.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 08:23:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot qualification recap — recommendations, perf links, and next steps

Ari — thanks, good questions. Answers below and items we can commit to for the pilot: 

1) TPS/latency characterization: the numbers in the PDF are end-to-end measurements (including tokenization and KV-cache handling) from a 48-hour spike test we ran with your payload profile (420 in / 120 out). The p95 ~360ms was observed at sustained 100–140 QPS with the continuous batching policy we propose. We’ll run an additional 6-hour stress test replaying your sample distribution once you share the synthetic set.

2) Data residency / deployment: Dedicated (reserved) in your us-east-1 VPC with AWS PrivateLink + customer-managed KMS will meet the compliance you described. Private (air-gapped) is only necessary for full on-prem installs or special legal requirements. We’ll include the network diagram and a short checklist in the SOW.

3) PHI handling: we can implement a two-step onboarding flow — (a) initial synthetic/sanitized prompt set for functional tuning and perf runs, (b) a redaction-only live pass inside your VPC where you control the de-identifier before any token leaves the VPC. Camila will run the onboarding playbook.

Cost estimate (high-level, pilot 3 weeks):
- Reserved baseline (8 gpus, burst policy): $32,400 (includes 10% buffer for burst capacity)
- Data egress estimate: $1,200 (depends on exact sample sizes)
- Engineering onboarding (one-time): $6,500
Estimated total: ~$40k (we can provide a detailed line-item SOW).

Attached I’ve included: benchmark-run-20271001.csv (raw metrics from the spike test). Also re-attached the perf-profile PDF and prompt set.

Next steps:
- Confirm pilot scope + approve estimate (you)
- Quick onboarding slot — Tue 5 Oct 10:30–11:00 ET or Wed 6 Oct 09:00–09:45 ET (Camila + Rishi + Ari)
- Once approved, I’ll circulate a short SOW and the VPC checklist for your security team.

Camila — can you take the lead on the onboarding runbook/secret exchange notes? Rishi — I’ll loop you in on the SOW.

Best,
Evelyn
